# `prefer-ends-with`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a length-guarded `std.mem.eql` comparison against the tail slice of the
same sequence.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`std.mem.endsWith` states the suffix predicate and owns the short-input
boundary.

## When it fires

The exact `haystack.len >= needle.len and eql(haystack[haystack.len -
needle.len..], needle)` shape is required. Unguarded slicing and computed bounds
are excluded.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn hasSuffix(text: []const u8, suffix: []const u8) bool {
    return text.len >= suffix.len and std.mem.eql(u8, text[text.len - suffix.len ..], suffix);
}
```
